Maya G: FYI I ran the nightly FP8 sweep on prod-like traces and noticed a regression after the latest calibration dataset change — P99 token latency up ~12% for long sequences (seq=2048) on bsz=1 streaming with KV warmup. Perf profile attached below.

Ashwin P: ugh. which kernel path? fp8 native or falling back to int8/4-bit emu?

Maya G: It looks like kernel selection is toggling between fp8-fast and fp8-fallback for ~30% of layers at warmup, then stabilizes. Warmup tail seems to interact badly with our batching jitter heuristic.

Jordan: can you paste the profiler snippet? quick grep of hot ops helps.

Maya G: sure — here's the critical excerpt from perf tool (trimmed):
```
Profile summary:
- forward_total: 312ms
- fp8-kernel-fast: 180ms (60%)
- fp8-kernel-fallback: 54ms (17%)  <-- higher per-op latency
- kv-cache-fill: 28ms
- batch-coalesce: 20ms
Hot layers: attn_qkv (fallback hopping at layer 10, 22, 34)
```

Samir: interesting. fallback usually means quantization mismatch (scale/zero-point) or unsupported op shape. Did calib produce per-tensor scales that fail for certain channels?

Maya G: I dug in — the layers with fallback had high outlier activation channels. Our per-tensor calibration masked those, so quantization range widened and kernel chooses safer slow-path.

Li: So this is a dataset selection issue. If calibration includes a few extreme outliers, per-tensor will blow up ranges and push kernels to fallback. Per-channel might isolate outliers but has quality tradeoffs.

Nina: proposal: try two-parallel experiments
1) per-channel calibration with 99.9 percentile clipping (trim top 0.1%)
2) per-tensor calibration but run an outlier-trim pass to remove top 0.5% activations per-layer before computing scale
We should measure both speed + lm-quality (perplexity + a small eval set).

Ashwin P: agree. Also test with synthetic micro-batches to exercise batching jitter: run seq=2048 bsz=1 with random arrival times (poisson) to see the scheduler decisions — our batching window & jitter may be merging KV warmup with steady-state in bad ways.

Jordan: can infra run the perf harness on dedicated gpux pool? want stable env. @infra-bot can you queue job with tags: fp8-calib-experiment, seed=42, traces=prod-aug-2025, seq=2048, bsz=1 x3 runs each config

infra-bot: job queued: fp8-calib-experiment-1723456789; estimated runtime 2h; nodes: 4 (A100-80G); notify: Maya G, Ashwin P, Samir.

Samir: quick note about quality: per-channel calibration historically improves numeric fidelity on narrow channels but increases memory for scale storage. For our runtime that is fine, but need to ensure kernel supports per-channel FP8 layout without degrading throughput (memory access pattern matters).

Maya G: right — one more wrinkle: the fallback detection logic currently checks "scaled_range > kernel_threshold" and then switches path mid-sequence. We could change it to sticky per-request selection to avoid oscillation — pick fastest compatible kernel at first token and stick to it for that request.

Li: sticky choice reduces oscillation but could hurt if range evolves (e.g., initial prompt short then long). Maybe make it sticky per-batch-window, or allow a single mid-stream switch only if stable for N tokens.

Ashwin P: let's avoid big control-flow changes for now. Short-term: try per-channel + clip and per-tensor + outlier-trim, plus a variant with sticky-kernel toggle disabled (force no mid-stream switch) to see delta.

Nina: I'll assemble calibration datasets: 1) baseline (current sweep) 2) trimmed (remove locs with >99.5 percentile activations) 3) per-channel-sampled (stratified across seq lengths and tail prompts). Will push to /calib/runs/1723456789/

Jordan: add evaluation metrics we need: latency P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, model perplexity on eval-1000, accuracy on nudge prompt set, and kernel-selection counts (.fast vs .fallback). Also capture KV-cache fill times across first 64 tokens.

Maya G: thanks. If perf reg reproduces we should revert the last calibration sweep in prod and roll a conservative profile until we have results. I opened a quick rollback PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/PR-4021

Samir: also flag to product/observability — small perf regressions can cascade to SLOs. @Nina can you add a note in #eng-sre if we see >5% P99 regression in canary?

Nina: yea will do. I'll post results in this thread when infra finishes.

Ashwin P: TL;DR action items: (1) run 3 calibration configs (per-channel+clip, per-tensor+trim, baseline) (2) toggle sticky kernel flag experiment (3) perf + quality evals on seq=2048 streaming traces (4) block rollback if regressions confirmed

Maya G: perfect. Ping me when job completes. Thanks all :thumbsup:
